blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Despite recent progress in handwritten text recognition, medieval Arabic scientific manuscripts remain an open challenge for current vision-language models (VLMs) due to cursive ligatures, variable diacritization, and more importantly the lack of training data. This paper aims to address this gap, by proposing the first annotation guidelines dedicated to the transcription of scientific Arabic manuscripts inspired by textual criticism, a well-established approach to historical text editing. We then propose, ATHAAR, a new dataset manually annotated following this guideline. Unlike previous resources in the field, ATHAAR varies both witnesses of the same text, calligraphic styles, and content to deal with texts but also numerals. Relying on state-of-the-art VLMs, we finally design a set of experiments to study models transfer across scripts, chapters, and treatises. Our findings highlight the limitations of current systems when faced with the specificities of ancient scientific texts.
blocks.zh: 尽管最近在手写文字识别方面取得了进展,但中世纪的阿拉伯科学手稿仍然对当前视觉语言模型(VLMs)来说是一个公开的挑战,因为咒语结扎,可变的二化,更重要的是缺乏培训数据. 本文旨在弥补这一差距,提出第一个专门对受到文字批评的阿拉伯科学手稿进行抄录的说明准则,这是历史文字编辑的既定办法。 然后,我们提议,ATHAAR公司根据这项准则,采用人工附加说明的新数据集。 与之前的字段资源不同,ATHAAR既不同于同一文本的目击者,书法风格,也不同于处理文本的内容,但也不同于数字. 依靠最先进的VLM,我们最终设计了一套实验来研究跨脚本,章节和论文的模型转移. 我们的研究结果突出了在面对古代科学文本的特殊性时,现有系统的局限性。

blocks.en:
As our study focuses on historical manuscripts, a closer analysis of existing HTR datasets reveals three main limitations for our use case:
(1) Under-representation of the scientific domain. Available resources are composed of religious (such as Agapet ( Ibrahim, 2024 ) , and Historical Arabic HTR Najam and Faizullah (2024) ), literary texts (e.g., Iskandar LiPA and Huma-Num (2024) , RASAM Vidal-Gorène et al. (2021a) ). These datasets are therefore not suited to deal with texts such as those found in the exact sciences, where domain-specific terminology, numerals and geometrical
objects (e.g., angles) compound the challenges of automatic recognition.
(2) Lack of annotation guidelines. Annotation conventions guiding manual transcription are rarely
documented and none report inter-annotators agreement raising questions about their reliability for evalutaing, training or fine-tuning HTR models.
(3) Limited diversity in scripts and textual witnesses. Variability in writing styles across manuscripts of the same text is limited. Indeed, to ensure stable learning and avoid biases (such as overfitting to a single scribe), HTR models must be exposed to a variety of handwriting styles for the same content.

Recent work falls into two groups. The first
covers printed and modern handwritten Arabic. Qalam ( Bhatia et al., 2024 ) is a multimodal model fine-tuned on printed
benchmarks and synthetic data generated from modern Arabic books.
Qari-OCR-2B ( Wasfy et al., 2025 ) follows a similar approach, fine-tuning Qwen-2-VL-2B using a synthetic pipeline that renders text from modern news and classical Islamic corpora in twelve Arabic fonts. The second group targets handwritten and historical text. HATFormer ( Chan et al., 2025 ) fine-tunes a TrOCR-based architecture on
synthetic line images and Muharaf ( Saeed et al., 2024 ) , a corpus of 19th–21st century documents. CHURRO-3B ( Semnani et al., 2025 ) is a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct on historical manuscripts across multiple languages. Arabic training data comes from existing datasets including Muharaf, RASAM and RASM for a total of 2,367 pages. None of these datasets covers scientific manuscripts, with specificities
such as script variation and multiple witnesses of the same text.

Our dataset is composed of a set of scientific manuscripts sampled from different authors. Our main source is al-Qānūn al-Mas‘ūdī , an
astronomical treatise composed by al-Bīrūnī around 1035 which
is organized into eleven books, each divided into chapters. Four of the manuscripts
of the Qānūn manuscripts are available
online, while the remaining copies were acquired from the holding libraries as part of the preparation of a critical edition of the Qānūn Loizelet (2021) .
In addition, the corpus also includes other scientific treatises from the same period covering astronomy and mathematics. To mitigate the risk of training-data contamination, we prioritized the collection of manuscript witnesses not publicly accessible online.

blocks.en:
Prior to the annotation process, the digital copies of each manuscript underwent
five pre-processing steps:
(1) rotation correction to align pages;
(2) conversion to JPG format for compatibility with the annotation
platform (see below);
(3) page splitting, separating double-page scans into individual folios;
(4) image cropping to a consistent resolution within each manuscript; and
(5) scheduling of annotation batches by manuscript difficulty, grouping
witnesses with high diacritization rates, dense digit strings, or
significant physical degradation (ink fading, bleed-through) into
dedicated weekly sessions to allow annotators to calibrate their
judgement progressively.
Annotation is performed at the line level, following the PAGE-XML standard ( Pletschacher and Antonacopoulos, 2010 ) promoted by the PRImA
Research Lab, which is the de facto granularity for HTR evaluation.

blocks.en: 4.4 Annotation Procedure
blocks.zh: 4.4 注释程序

blocks.en:
Annotators followed a written guide, provided in Appendix B.1 and in the supplementary material. It was written for Arabic scientific manuscripts, drawing on the
principles of diplomatic editing ( West, 1973 ) : faithful
reproduction of what the scribe wrote without correcting, modernizing the spelling or
interpreting the content, preservation of domain-specific
notation (numerals, geometrical objects), and
explicit rules for every element that deviates from running prose. The
critical edition of Loizelet (2021) served as the textual reference,
supplying the authoritative reading against which each transcribed line
is aligned. The same guide was applied uniformly across all tiers.
blocks.zh:
注释员遵循一份书面指南,载于附录B.1和补充材料。 这是为阿拉伯科学手稿而写的,借鉴了
外交编辑原则(西方,1973年):忠实
复制文士所写的,不作更正,使拼写现代化或
解释内容、特定域的保护
注(数字、几何物体),以及
明确的规则 每一个元素偏离 运行的散文。 这个
Loizelet(2021年)的批判版作为文本参考,
提供每个转录行的权威性读数
对齐。 同一指南统一适用于所有级别。

blocks.en:
Annotators are asked to transcribe each line directly from the image
, in
reading order, from top to bottom and right to left. To reduce complexity due to layout (cf. Section 4.1 ), only the titles and main text are transcribed.
Running headers, page footers, page and folio numbers, independent marginal notes (additions, glosses, comments), tables, diagrams, ornaments and library stamps are excluded, and regions detected automatically in these categories are deleted. One exception applies: when a word begun in the main text is completed in the margin, the two fragments are joined in the transcription of that line, and the line polygon is extended to include the margin fragment.

请注释者直接从图像中转录每行
时
从上到下,从右到左。 为了减少由于布局(参见第4.1节)而产生的复杂程度,只转录标题和正文.
正在运行的页眉、页脚、页码和页码、独立的边注(添加、缩写、注释)、表格、图表、装饰品和图书室邮票除外,在这些类别中自动检测的区域被删除。 一个例外适用:当正文开始的单词在边框中完成时,将两个片段合并在该行的抄写中,并将线条多边形延伸至包括边框片段.

blocks.en: Regarding diacritics and vowel signs, they are transcribed when the scribe wrote them and are never added elsewhere. Finally, scientific manuscripts contain many numerical values, often overlined. A numeral the annotator can read is transcribed. Otherwise the annotator inserts a tag naming its numeral system (e.g., [indian_numbers] ), or an unknown-system tag (e.g., [unknown_numbers] ) when the system cannot be identified. Other overlined elements that denote geometrical objects receive their own tag (e.g., [geometrical_object] ). Damaged or illegible text is replaced by a tag (e.g., [unreadable] ), either within the line or for the whole line (see details in Appendix B.1.1 ).

blocks.en: We used Calfa Vision 3 3 3 https://vision.calfa.fr ( Vidal-Gorène et al., 2021a ) , a web platform for assisted transcription of handwritten and printed documents for three reasons: it provides a generic layout model for historical Arabic manuscripts, whose output the annotator corrects instead of drawing lines from scratch; it was already used to build Arabic manuscript datasets such as RASAM ( Vidal-Gorène et al., 2021b ) and it exports PAGE-XML, the format of most datasets in Table 1 . The transcription rules do not depend on the tool: any editor that exports PAGE-XML can apply them. The tool is illustrated in Figure 3 , Appendix B .

Annotation was carried out by two authors of this paper which are native Arabic speakers with expertise in medieval Arabic manuscripts, under the supervision of an expert in Arabic philology, following a three steps procedure. In the first training phase , each annotator independently transcribed 8 pages from Tier 1 (Ms04, Ms05, Ms07, Ms10, Ms14 and Ms15)
using Calfa Vision and following the annotation guide. The supervisor reviewed the results, provided corrections and feedback, and confirmed that both annotators had reached a sufficient understanding of the
guide before moving to the next step.

blocks.en: In the adjudication phase , both annotators independently transcribed the same 4 pages - one per manuscript, across Ms01, Ms02, Ms13 and Ms17 (127 lines) corresponding to 4% of the total lines of Tiers 1 + 2. These pages have been chosen as they contain full text without any additional content (tables, diagrams), covering more text and making the results comparable. The agreement between the two transcriptions was then computed and is reported in Section 5.1 . The supervisor verified that the agreement metrics were satisfactory before authorizing the full annotation.

blocks.en:
In the full annotation phase , each page image was first checked for sharpness, completeness and orientation. Text regions
and line baselines were then detected automatically by Calfa Vision’s
built-in layout analysis model. The annotator removed out-of-scope regions, merged or split
regions, and corrected missing, merged or misplaced baselines; line polygons were then computed from the corrected baselines and checked visually. Finally, the annotator transcribed at the line level.
Each manuscript was exported as PAGE-XML, which stores the baseline, the polygon and the Unicode transcription of every line, together with the exact page images so that coordinates and images remain aligned.
Annotation proceeded in weekly batches, and the supervisor validated each batch before the next one was assigned.

blocks.en: 6.2 Models and Settings
blocks.zh: 6.2 模型和设置

blocks.en:
We evaluated several models from three families (general-purpose multimodal models, Arabic-oriented VLMs, and OCR-specialized VLMs) but only reports the best preforming ones: (1) Gemini 3 Flash ( Google DeepMind, 2025 ) a general-purpose VLM optimized for
speed and long-context processing. (2) CHURRO-3B ( Semnani et al., 2025 ) an open-weights VLM for historical document transcription in 46 languages, including Arabic.
(3) Qari-OCR-2B ( Wasfy et al., 2025 ) a VLM fine-tuned
specifically for Arabic text recognition.
blocks.zh:
我们评价了来自三个家庭的几个模式(通用多式联运模式、面向阿拉伯语的甚高频和OCR专业的甚高频),但只报告了最佳的预构模式: (1)双子座3 Flash(Google DeepMind, 2025) 通用VLM 优化用于
速度和长文本处理. (2) CHURRO-3B(Semnani等人,2025年),是历史文件的46种语言(包括阿拉伯语)的可公开加权的VLM。
(3) Qari-OCR-2B(Wasfy等人,2025年) VLM微调
特别是阿拉伯文文本识别。

blocks.en:
Models receive as input line crops, as extracted from the PAGE-XML
annotations using the polygon coordinates of each TextLine element.
They are prompted in English, preliminary experiments with Arabic prompts were not conclusive.

使用每个文本线元素的多边形坐标的说明。
他们用英语进行诱导,但用阿拉伯语诱导的初步实验没有结论。

blocks.en:
We run each model in both zero-shot and few-shot settings (see Appendix C.4 for an ablation study).
We report the average CER and WER across 3 runs after normalizing models outputs and the reference annotation (ground truth) following the standard protocol in the field: redundant blank characters are collapsed;
 special characters are removed;
 Numbers are normalized to their Arabic-Indic equivalents; and
 any characters outside the Arabic script are removed. An important pre-processing prior to evaluation was removing tatweel (elongation). Indeed, scribal elongation can trigger runaway
generation: in one C-Ch line, the scribe’s extended tatweel led Gemini to generate 4,037 characters instead of 11, a single error that alone raised its CER on C-Ch from 18.9% to 74.3%, illustrating
why normalization before scoring is necessary. Table 4 reports our results.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
This work introduced Athaar , the first manually
annotated dataset with a documented annotation guide for medieval Arabic
scientific manuscript recognition, and the only historical Arabic dataset
offering multi-witness transcriptions of the same text. We built a
multi-tiered corpus of 3,893 lines
and evaluated state-of-the-art models in three
transfer scenarios: same chapter across different scribal hands,
same manuscript across different chapters, and chapters from different treatises
entirely.
blocks.zh:
这部作品引入了Athaar,
附有中世纪阿拉伯语注释指南的注解数据集
科学手稿的识别, 以及唯一的阿拉伯历史数据集
提供同一文本的多证人记录。 我们造了一个
3,893行的多层集合
并评价了三种最新模式
转录假想:同一章跨越不同的斜手,
不同章节的相同手稿和不同论文的章节
完全一样

blocks.en:
Our results show that general-purpose VLMs such as Gemini 3 Flash
dominate the current state of the art but still lag significantly as
manuscript complexity increases - ligatures, tatweel - even when support images are
provided. Models fine-tuned on the HTR task, by contrast, struggle to
reliably transcribe lines without hallucinating or omitting words.
blocks.zh:
我们的结果显示,通用的VLM,比如双子座3闪电
主导当前状态,但仍明显滞后,如
手稿复杂度增加 - 粘结、 tatweel - 即使支持图像是
提供。 对比之下,对HTR任务进行微调的模型
可靠地转换线条而不产生幻觉或省略文字.

blocks.en:
Looking ahead, two directions appear most promising: fine-tuning
open-weights VLMs on Athaar with training strategies that balance
performance across scripts and content types; and developing methods that
explicitly model calligraphic specificities that remain beyond the reach of current
models. Finally, beyond HTR, Athaar opens directions for two further tasks: line segmentation , supported by ground-truth polygon coordinates, and script identification , leveraging multi-witness
contrasts between Naskh and Nasta’liq .

Athaar上的具有平衡培训战略的VLM

Naskh和Nastaliq之间的对比。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
This study has several limitations. First, the corpus is limited to a authors from the same period, restricting generalization to the
broader landscape of medieval Arabic scientific manuscripts. Expanding Athaar to other authors, disciplines, and manuscript traditions is a
natural next step.
blocks.zh:
这项研究有若干局限性。 首先,本文书仅限于同一时期的作者,将一般规定限于
更广阔的中世纪阿拉伯科学手稿景观. 将Athaar扩展至其他作者、学科和手稿传统是一种
自然的下一步。

blocks.en:
Furthermore, while we evaluate both zero-shot and
few-shot settings, no fine-tuning experiments are conducted; supervised
or semi-supervised approaches will need to be explored to fully capture
the potential of domain-adapted models.

blocks.en:
Figure 1 contrasts three writing contexts to illustrate the domain gap that motivates Athaar .
Figure 1(a) shows a modern arabic text: characters are uniform, spacing is regular, and
diacritics are placed consistently.
Figure 1(b) shows modern handwritten Arabic ( Mahmoud et al., 2012 ) : letterforms vary between writers, but the script remains familiar to current OCR and HTR systems trained on modern data.
Figure 1(c) shows an excerpt from Ms01 (12th c., Berlin, Or-Quart-1613): the scribe uses prolonged tatweel strokes that extend words horizontally, mixes numeral strings with dense cursive text, and employs a calligraphic hand that has no direct equivalent in modern training corpora.
The visual distance between Figure 1(a) and
Figure 1(c) explains why models trained or evaluated on modern Arabic fail to transfer to medieval scientific manuscripts.
blocks.zh:
图1对比了三个写作背景来说明激发Athaar的域间隙.

blocks.en: Few-shot prompt You transcribe single lines from historical Arabic scientific manuscripts. Task : write exactly what the scribe wrote on the line in the TEST IMAGE. 1. Do not correct, normalize or modernize it. 2. Write diacritics (vowel signs, shadda, sukun) only where they are visible. Never add them. 3. Write hamza and letter dots only as they appear in the image. 4. Write numerals with Eastern Arabic-Indic digits (e.g. 0--9 rendered in their Arabic-Indic form). 5. If a word is illegible, skip it. Never guess or complete it from context. 6. Output only the transcription of the TEST IMAGE, on one line: no translation, explanation, quotes or formatting.
